thread:
sam.k: Heads-up — nightly perf job flagged a regression on the 16k-seq microbench. Median latency up ~35% vs last good run. https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4521 (perf-summary attached)
maria.p: ugh. is this on main? any rollout in last 24h?
perf-bot: nightly/perf-16k-seq #4521 FAILED
perf-bot: baseline: 120ms/token, current: 162ms/token (+35%), p99 also shifted
elaine: looks recent — I see mergers touching runtime/attention/heuristic.cc and runtime/scheduler/batching.cc in the last two days
ryan: can someone run a quick local repro? CI artifacts show perf numbers but we need a deterministic microbench
sam.k: trying local repro now:
```
./eng-runtime/tools/microbench --model=ggml-13b --seq=16384 --iters=20 --tag=nightly-repro
```
sam.k: baseline (from good commit): 118ms/token
sam.k: current HEAD: 160ms/token
sam.k: reproduces locally for me
tanvi: ok start a git bisect. I'll help triage commits touching attention path selection
maria.p: bisect plan: git bisect start HEAD <good-commit-sha>
maria.p: then run the microbench above as the test script
elaine: I've got a suspicion — commit a1b2c3d changed kernel selection to prefer the "scalar-attn" path for odd sequence lengths to avoid a kernel fusion bug. That could force a slower kernel on long seqs
ryan: fine, let's bisect. I kicked off:
```
git bisect start 1772510000 a9f8e7d
# running test: eng-runtime/tools/microbench --model=ggml-13b --seq=16384
```
ryan: bisect landed quickly — candidate range narrowed to three commits: a1b2c3d, b2c3d4e, c3d4e5f
tanvi: can you paste the perf numbers per commit? even a quick median helps
ryan: a1b2c3d -> 158ms/token
ryan: b2c3d4e -> 161ms/token
ryan: c3d4e5f -> 119ms/token (good)
sam.k: so the regression appears introduced at a1b2c3d
elaine: that's the attention-path heuristic commit I mentioned. It toggles preference when seq length % 512 < 32 (we had a weird corner case)
maria.p: any profiler output? flame graphs or nvprof/kerneltimer?
sam.k: I ran a quick CPU profile and got heavy time spent in kernel 'attn_scalar' vs previous 'attn_fused' — sample:
```
# profile top stack (sample counts)
attn_scalar         76%
kv_cache_lookup     8%
batching_sched      6%
others               10%
```
sam.k: so runtime is choosing scalar path a lot
elaine: patch at a1b2c3d (summary: "heuristic: prefer scalar on odd tails to avoid device sync") — maybe the guard is too aggressive and triggers for long sequences
tanvi: can we try flipping the heuristic locally to see perf impact? quick patch to fallback to fused unless explicit bug trigger
ryan: applied a local revert of the heuristic, re-ran microbench -> 120ms/token (back to baseline)
ryan: proof attached (cli output)
sam.k: nice. So root cause is heuristic change. Is there a known correctness bug that motivated it?
elaine: yes there was a rare deadlock on specific GPU kernels on older drivers (reported 1 time internally). The heuristic was a pragmatic stopgap but it wasn't tested on high seq lengths
maria.p: plan options: 1) revert heuristic entirely (safe for perf) 2) narrow heuristic to specific driver version/device id 3) add explicit test to catch perf regressions + CI block
tanvi: for immediate rollout-blocker we should revert the heuristic in main and cut a quick hotfix revert PR. Then open a follow-up to implement targeted fix and add tests
sam.k: I'll open PR to revert a1b2c3d: PR #4578 — "revert: heuristic-change avoid scalar-attn preference" — draft created, needs eng-runtime review
sam.k: tagging @elaine @ryan for quick review
elaine: reviewing now. Also adding a short perf unit test that runs microbench (low-iterations) to detect large regressions on PRs
maria.p: add CI perf gate as an experimental check (non-blocking for now) — but for rollouts we'll enforce it until we reintroduce a less-regressive fix
deploy-bot: rollout blocked for release/2026-03-18 due to perf spike on main
ryan: after revert in my local, I re-ran full profile: attn_fused back to 70% samples, latency recovered
sam.k: PR #4578 merged to main (revert of a1b2c3d). I'll monitor nightly job
perf-bot: nightly/perf-16k-seq #4524 STARTED
maria.p: thanks everyone. Follow-up action items:
- (elaine) postmortem + root-cause writeup (include driver bug reproducer)
- (sam.k) keep the perf microbench in CI experimental suite
- (tanvi) draft targeted heuristic that checks driver/device id rather than sequence tail
sam.k: closing thread once nightly confirms numbers. early numbers show main is back to baseline. :thumbsup:
__notes: This file models a short Slack bisect coordination thread for a perf regression caused by an attention-path heuristic change. Messages are intentionally concise, with command snippets and small logs.
